title: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics — Current Population Survey concepts and definitions
use: Scoped U.S. population, employment, unemployment, participation, search and ongoing-duration definitions; no current unemployment release or data imported.
verification: Opened actual official page and inspected base population and employment/unemployment/search sections, labor-force and employment-population denominators, not-in-labor-force classification and the duration section distinguishing ongoing from completed spells. Benefit receipt is explicitly irrelevant to statistical unemployment classification. All numerical counts and model hazards are original synthetic cases. This is not a cross-country definition catalogue.

title: Daron Acemoglu, MIT 14.661 — Lectures 11–13: Search, Matching and Unemployment (December 2017)
use: Primary teaching reference for the flow, matching, vacancy-value and bargaining mechanisms. Chapter derives its own discrete-time model, probability domain and synthetic equilibria.
verification: Retrieved the actual 105-page official PDF. Inspected slides34–56 (PDF pages34–56): continuous-time constant-returns matching, tightness and arrival intensities, separation flow balance, Beveridge relation, vacancy and job Bellman equations, free entry and pair-specific Nash bargaining. The source's continuous-time rates and capital assumptions are not transplanted into the chapter's discrete model. Formula extraction has formatting imperfections; the original chapter equations are independently derived with explicit dated cash flows, without reproducing source formulas or numerical cases. No source empirical claim or entire-course verification asserted.

title: Daron Acemoglu, MIT 14.661 — Lecture7: Efficiency Wages (November2017)
use: Primary teaching route to moral hazard, employment rents, nonshirking incentives and their aggregate labor-demand connection; original discrete-time proof and examples supplied in manuscript.
verification: Opened actual27-page official PDF and read slides2–18: effort not contractible from aggregate output, limited punishment instruments, continuous-time detection/separation intensities, worker value equations, nonshirking condition and stationary labor-demand closure. Read caution about nonstationary reasoning and contract timing. Extracted continuous-time formulas are not copied; our conditional discrete detection probability and Bellman inequalities are independently derived. Source welfare claims and historical numerical estimates are not imported.

title: Olivier J.Blanchard and Lawrence H.Summers — Hysteresis in Unemployment, NBER WorkingPaper2035 (October1986)
use: Strict versus broader persistence concept; membership and duration mechanisms as theoretical possibilities. Original bounded threshold example is distinct from the paper's model and estimates.
verification: Downloaded the actual public PDF after browser PDF extraction failed; read local pdftotext output for title/date, abstract, introduction and strict-versus-loose terminology footnote, section4 on duration and the conclusion with qualifications. The paper discusses membership and duration mechanisms, warns that complete persistence in its simplified duration argument is too strong, and calls for further development/testing. No historical macro observations, coefficients or policy prescription from this1986 paper are represented as October2026 evidence.
